collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: answering service missing about 10 calls/week; ~40% could have been bookings; missed calls during business hours when staff is busy with patients; tried an AI last year and it was garbage; mis-handled patient questions; failed to book properly; sounded unnatural; wasted three months

transcript:
User: Hi. Saw your ad. Honestly I doubt this is for us but go ahead.
Agent: Got it—so you saw our ad, makes sense to be skeptical. What about it caught your attention enough to call?
User: Just curious. But we already have an answering service, so not sure why we'd need this.
Agent: Yeah, totally fair—if you’ve already got an answering service, the only reason to change is if calls are still slipping through or not turning into booked jobs. What’s the one thing your answering service *doesn’t* do well today?
User: They miss about 10 calls a week, and I think around 40% of those could've been bookings.
Agent: Got it—missing about 10 calls a week and ~40% could’ve been bookings is a lot of money sitting on the table. When those calls get missed, is it mostly during business hours while you’re busy, or after-hours?
User: Mostly during business hours when we're busy with patients. But what’s this going to cost? Give me a number now or I'm done.
Agent: I hear you—you don’t want a runaround. We don’t have one flat price because it depends on call volume and what you want it to handle, but most clinics land in the **$1,200–$2,800/month** range. If I tell you a number inside that range, what would feel like “okay, keep talking” for you?
User: Alright, that range is reasonable. But how do I know you won't disappear with our patient data?
Agent: Makes sense—patient data is non‑negotiable. Are you mainly worried about **HIPAA/BAA compliance**, or about **where the call recordings/transcripts are stored and who can access them**?
User: Both, really. I need to know you're solid on compliance and data security before considering this.
Agent: Absolutely—both are valid. Do you require a signed **BAA** as a must-have?
User: Yes, a signed BAA is non-negotiable. We have to ensure HIPAA compliance and protect our patient data.
Agent: Got it—BAA is a must. We can sign a BAA, and we lock down access, encryption, and retention so only approved users can see anything; Jay (our founder) will walk you through the exact safeguards on a quick call. Before that, mind if I do a 30‑second calculation on what those missed calls are likely costing you each week?
User: Alright, go ahead. But just so you know, I tried one of these AI things last year and it was garbage.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—there’s a lot of junk out there. So just to run the math: ballpark, how many calls a week are hitting voicemail or getting missed—still around 10?
User: Yes, about 10 calls a week get missed. But I need assurance this won't waste our time like before.
Agent: Totally fair—I’d want that too. For the quick math, what’s your average appointment value in dollars—are we talking more like **$200, $400, or $800**?
User: Our average appointment value is around $700. But I need to know this AI won’t be garbage again.
Agent: Got it—so with 10 missed calls a week, 40% booking rate, and $700 average value, that’s about **$2800 extra a week** you’re missing… and that’s roughly **$12100/mo**. Does that sound about right?

And on the “garbage AI” concern—what specifically went wrong last time: did it mis-handle patient questions, fail to book, or just sound unnatural?
User: It mis-handled patient questions and failed to book properly. Sounded unnatural, too. Wasted three months.
Agent: Yeah—that would make anyone swear off it. What we do differently is we map the exact patient questions you get, keep it tightly within approved answers, and only book when it has the right details… so it doesn’t “wing it” and mess up.

Cool—it's a 20-minute walkthrough with Jay this week so you can hear it handle real patient scenarios and see what $12.1k/mo recovered could look like. What’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, I'll try it. Let's book the live call for tomorrow afternoon. Confirm my best number is +16025550017.
Agent: Got it—yes, we’ll use the number you’re calling from ending in **0017**. What’s your first name?
User: Brenda. Looking forward to seeing how this works out. Confirmed for tomorrow afternoon.
Agent: Love it, Brenda—thank you. What’s your last name?
User: Kowalski. Looking forward to the call and seeing if this can really make a difference for us.
Agent: Got it, Brenda Kowalski. What’s the name of your clinic?
User: It's Desert Bloom Dental, located in Phoenix, Arizona. Looking forward to seeing how your service can help us.
Agent: Perfect—Desert Bloom Dental. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: We're in Arizona time — we don't do daylight saving here. So, effectively Mountain time. See you tomorrow.
Agent: Perfect—Mountain time, got it. For tomorrow afternoon, I can do **1:30 PM** or **2:15 PM** Mountain time—which works?
User: 2:15 PM Arizona time works for us. Looking forward to it. Thanks for accommodating our schedule.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Brenda—you're all set for **tomorrow at 2:15 PM Arizona time**. You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details—you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, take your time. Just let me know once you're all set for tomorrow afternoon.
Agent: All set, Brenda—tomorrow at 2:15 PM Arizona time is confirmed, and you’ll get an SMS with the details shortly. Really glad you called—Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
